title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy Version 1.0
quote: With this document we are making a public commitment to a concrete framework for managing these risks—one that will evolve over time, but that seeks to establish clear expectations and accountability in its initial form.

title: Responsible Scaling Policy
quote: a public commitment not to train or deploy models capable of causing catastrophic harm unless we have implemented safety and security measures that will keep risks below acceptable levels

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 2.1
quote: This update clarifies which Capability Thresholds would require enhanced safeguards beyond our current ASL-3 standards.

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 2.2
quote: This update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.

title: Activating AI Safety Level 3 protections
quote: We are deploying Claude Opus 4 with our ASL-3 measures as a precautionary and provisional action.

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.0
quote: This update is a comprehensive rewrite of our RSP.

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.1
quote: This revision addresses the following points: (1) how we operationalize the Automated R&D capability threshold; (2) how we use internal feedback on Risk Reports

title: Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy
quote: After we released the v3 update, readers noted two areas on which our language could be clarified.

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.2
quote: This update authorizes the LTBT to request external review of Risk Reports, gives the LTBT the power to approve our selection of external reviewers

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.3
quote: This update (1) revises our threshold for novel chemical/biological weapons production to better track the threat model of concern

title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.4
quote: It now requires that fully unredacted Risk Reports be shared with at least 200 Anthropic employees, rather than with all regular-clearance Anthropic staff.

title: Zach Stein-Perlman argues Anthropic misdescribed an RSP ambiguity that was in fact a missed ASL-3 threshold
quote: far as I can tell, this description is wrong; it was not an ambiguity; the RSP set forth an ASL-3 threshold and the Claude 3 Opus evals report incorrectly asserted that that threshold was merely a yellow line.

title: SaferAI argues the October 2024 RSP update is a step backwards
quote: However, this approach is susceptible to shifting goalposts as capabilities advance.

title: Garrison Lovely argues Anthropic quietly dropped its commitment to define ASL-4 before releasing an ASL-3 model
quote: Yet the company's latest RSP, updated May 14, doesn't publicly define ASL-4 — despite treating Claude 4 Opus as an ASL-3 model.

title: TIME reports Anthropic is dropping the central pledge of its Responsible Scaling Policy
quote: the change to the RSP leaves Anthropic far less constrained by its own safety policies

title: METR policy director Chris Painter says RSP v3 signals Anthropic is shifting into triage mode
quote: believes it needs to shift into triage mode with its safety plans, because methods to assess and mitigate risk are not keeping up with the pace of capabilities

title: The Midas Project logs RSP v3 as a major, undisclosed revocation of a core RSP component
quote: Anthropic Major Change Not disclosed No Feb 24, 2026 Revoked a core component of their Responsible Scaling Policy

title: Transparency Coalition argues Anthropic’s stated reason for dropping its core safety principle makes no sense
quote: Anthropic says it is abandoning its core safety principle in order to make the world more safe.

title: GovAI argues dropping the pause commitment makes unacceptable-risk deployments more likely
quote: Dropping the pause commitment makes it more likely Anthropic will deploy models with unacceptable risks.

title: Zvi argues RSP v3 abandons many previous commitments, including not moving ahead when dangerous
attributed_to: Zvi (Don’t Worry About the Vase; LessWrong)
quote: The changes involved include abandoning many previous commitments, including one not to move ahead if doing so would be dangerous

title: Louis Yiven Zhu finds Anthropic’s largest RSP revision, 2.2 to 3.0, was not redlined and mostly silent on its material changes
quote: Anthropic alone publishes redlines, for five of its seven revisions, yet its largest revision, from version 2.2 to 3.0, is one it did not redline
